cards.text: Twenty years. That's how long Solomon, king of Israel and son of David, has spent building the house of the LORD and his own palace. TWENTY YEARS, friend! I left dough in the fridge so long once it started paying rent, and even I never hit twenty years.

cards.question: Hiram, king of Tyre, had given Solomon some cities. What does Solomon do with them?

answers.text: Rebuilds them and settles Israelites there
Hands them back to Hiram as a gift
Leaves them empty and falling apart

cards.text: Next, Solomon goes to a city called Hamath-zobah. And I promise you, friend, he is NOT stopping by to drop off a cookie box.

cards.question: When Solomon goes to Hamath-zobah, he captures it.

cards.text: Then the building list just keeps going: Tadmor in the wilderness, store cities, cities for his chariots and horses, and Upper and Lower Beth-horon fortified with walls, gates and bars. Whatever he desired to build in Jerusalem, Lebanon and all through his land, it's on the list. Me? I fold ONE cookie box and I need to sit down.
Now, about the people still left in the land from the Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites. They're not Israelites.

cards.question: What does Solomon do with the descendants of those nations still in the land?

answers.text: Sends them out of the land

cards.question: Solomon puts the Israelites to slave labor too.
Solomon keeps the Israelites out of slave labor. Instead, they're his men of ___.

cards.text: Those Israelites lead his captains, command his chariots and cavalry, and serve as his chief officers: TWO HUNDRED FIFTY supervisors! My whole bakery has ONE supervisor, and it's the oven timer yelling at me every eleven minutes.
Then Solomon brings his wife, the daughter of Pharaoh, king of Egypt, up from the City of David. He moves her into a palace he built just for her.

cards.question: Solomon says his wife, Pharaoh's daughter, must not live in the house of David. Why not?

answers.text: The places the ark has entered are holy
The house of David is set apart for the Levites
The house of David is kept for the king's mighty men

cards.text: At that time, Solomon offers burnt offerings to the LORD on the altar he built in front of the portico. Cities, chariots, palaces, a whole kingdom to run, and the man STILL stops to worship the LORD.

cards.question: Solomon keeps the daily requirement for offerings according to the commandment of ___.
Besides Sabbaths and New Moons, Solomon keeps the three annual appointed feasts. Which of these is one of them?

cards.text: Next, Solomon sets up the temple crew: priests in divisions over their service, Levites to offer praise and minister before the priests, and gatekeepers by divisions at each gate. That's not just a temple anymore, friend, that's a WORK SCHEDULE.

cards.question: Solomon sets up the priests, Levites and gatekeepers this way because it was the command of ___, the man of God.
How closely is King Solomon's command about the priests and the Levites followed?

answers.text: Without turning aside in any matter
In every matter except the treasuries
Only in matters on the feast days

cards.question: From the day the foundation was laid, all of Solomon's work is carried out until the house of the LORD is completed.

cards.text: Then Solomon goes to Ezion-geber and Eloth, on the coast of Edom. Twenty years of building, and NOW the man goes to the coast.

cards.question: Out on the coast of Edom, who sends Solomon ships and crews of experienced sailors?
Hiram's sailors go with Solomon's servants to ___ and get gold there.

cards.text: They deliver 450 talents of gold to King Solomon, FOUR HUNDRED FIFTY! The fanciest thing in my old junk drawer was a coupon that expired years ago.

findings.problem: The opening story card has four sentences: 'Twenty years.', the explanation of Solomon's building, 'TWENTY YEARS, friend!', and the dough joke. That exceeds the opening-card limit.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has at least three sentences: two sentences about the building list and another for the cookie-box joke. The limit is two sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The phrase 'those nations' depends on the preceding story card for its meaning. The choice card itself never identifies the Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites, so it lacks the necessary context when shown on its own.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what.

findings.problem: The fill-in-the-blank cards at stop 1 card 9 and stop 2 cards 4, 7 and 12 ask for unseen answers—'war', 'Moses', 'David' and 'Ophir'—without earlier-card context from which those answers can be reasoned. They test wording recall or luck rather than inferable meaning.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Most of this stop's choices are unsupported discoveries rather than informed guesses. Cards 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9 and 12 give no earlier-card basis for determining Solomon's reason, Moses, the Feast of Weeks, David, the degree of obedience, the completion statement or Ophir. This goes beyond the permitted few discovery questions.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer. A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.
